behavior: A disabled `<fieldset>` disables each form part in it as its `disabled` prop does: `RadioGroup`, `Radio.Root`, `CheckboxGroup`, `Checkbox.Root`, `Switch.Root`, `NumberField`, `Select`, `Slider`, `OTPField`, `Combobox`, `Autocomplete`, `DateField`, `TimeField`, `DatePicker`, `DateRangePicker` and `TimePicker` with their popups, `Field.Root` and its parts, `Field.Item`, `Field.Control` (and `Input`) and `Fieldset.Root`. A native `<fieldset disabled>` counts as HTML disables a form control, except in its first `<legend>`, and `Fieldset.Root` with `disabled` counts also with no `Field.Root`. The parts then have `data-disabled`, and `aria-disabled` where the part sets it. A press, Space or a stepper button changes no value, Tab skips such a radio, checkbox or switch, the arrow keys skip such a radio, a radio group in such a fieldset has no tab stop, and `Form` leaves out the value of each such field. A native fieldset takes effect after the mount, and the parts follow each later change of it. Base UI follows only `Fieldset.Root` through `Field.Root`. In a native disabled fieldset, its parts show no disabled state, Tab focuses a radio, a checkbox or a switch, and a press or Space changes its value: the root dispatches a click to the disabled input, and the browser runs the listeners of a click that a script dispatches. A press on a Number Field stepper changes the value, because the press starts on `pointerdown`, and `Form` gives the value of each such field to `onFormSubmit`.
